newsitem.title: USA: Kinnard Q4 hurt by brokerage unit's revs.
newsitem.headline: Kinnard Q4 hurt by brokerage unit's revs.

text.p: Kinnard Investments Inc said on Friday its fourth-quarter results were hurt by an 11 percent decline in revenues at its John G. Kinnard and Co brokerage subsidiary.
The company also cited provisions for various claims and contingent liabilities, but Kinnard Investments treasurer Daniel Sass Sr told Reuters he would not discuss specifics.
"Our policy is not to get into specifics of individual cases that have no material impact on the financial position of the company," Sass said in a telephone interview.

Kinnard Investments late Thursday reported earnings for the quarter of $0.97 a share, including a gain on the sale of its PRIMEVEST Financial Services Inc unit. But without the gain, it incurred a loss of about $0.05 for the quarter compared to year-earlier profit of $0.11 a share.
Fourth-quarter total revenues were $25.2 million, up from $17.8 million.

"We're trying to become less dependent on the equity side of our business," said Sass, noting that performance among small cap stocks, which constitute much of the company's focus, did not perform as well as large cap stocks in the fourth quarter.

Sass said to remove some of the cyclicality from the company's revenue stream, it is targeting increasing its fixed-income presence to 16 percent from 10 percent. "We'd also like to see financial services grow. In the past year it was in the 12 to 13 percent range. We would like to get it to the 18 percent range (of our business)," he said.
Kinnard, a securities broker and investment banker, was trading off 7/8 at 5.
